lines: Bundles seven ordinary control signals into one MPX note stream, reading them all on the gate's rising edge and holding them for the life of the note
Sets the level of a note when nothing is patched to the level input, 0 to 100%
Sets the length of a note when nothing is patched to the duration input, 0.01 to 30 seconds, exponential so the short end has most of the travel
Sets the placing of a note across the stereo field when nothing is patched to the pan input, hard left to hard right
Declares how many semitones count as full bend deflection, 0 to 12, and travels with every note so the receiving end needs no matching setting; fractions are allowed
Chooses whether a note ends at its own duration whatever the gate does, or at whichever of the gate's fall and the duration comes first
A rising edge starts a note and the whole note is read at that instant; it reads high above 2V and low below 0.1V, and it is polyphonic, one note per channel
Sets the pitch of a note at its start, and afterwards any movement here is sent as bend measured from where the note began
Sets the level of a note, 0 to 10V mapping to none to full, read once at the note's start; the knob is used instead when nothing is patched
Sets the length of a note in seconds, one volt to the second, read once at the note's start; the knob is used instead when nothing is patched
Sets the placing of a note across the stereo field, -5V to 5V for hard left to hard right, read once at the note's start; the knob is used instead when nothing is patched
Sends pressure for a note that is already sounding, 0 to 10V, and with nothing patched here no pressure is sent at all rather than a stream of zeros
Sends timbre for a note that is already sounding, 0 to 10V, and with nothing patched here no timbre is sent at all rather than a stream of zeros
Carries the note stream to an MPX input; it is not a voltage, so a scope or a mixer reads nothing from it
Note — a bare gate makes a complete note, because every value not patched is taken from its knob
Note — the pitch read at the note's start is held for the life of the note, so a source that keeps moving afterwards bends the note instead of dragging it
Breaks an MPX note stream back out into seven ordinary signals, allocating the notes across a set number of voices
Sets how many voices the notes are shared between, 1 to 16, which is also the channel count of every output
Chooses what happens to a note that arrives with every voice busy: take the oldest, take the quietest, ignore it, glide within one voice, or play legato across two
Sets how long a glide takes, 0 to 2 seconds, and applies only in the two modes that reuse a sounding voice
Takes the note stream from an MPX output; it carries no voltage, so nothing else can be patched here usefully
Tells this module which voices are sounding, so a voice whose envelope has not finished is not taken for a new note
Carries a gate per voice for as long as that note lasts
Carries the pitch of each voice with any bend already added, so it can be patched straight to an oscillator
Carries the level each note was given, per voice
Carries the bend of each voice on its own, scaled by the bend range that travelled with the note
Carries pressure per voice, and stays where it was for a note whose source sent none
Carries timbre per voice, and stays where it was for a note whose source sent none
Carries the stereo placing of each voice
Note — every output is polyphonic with one channel per voice, so the voice count sets the channel count on all seven at once
Shows the notes going past on an MPX stream and the harmony they are played against, and passes the stream on unchanged
Freezes the display so a note that has gone past can be read
Takes the note stream from an MPX output
Carries the same stream on unchanged, so this can be placed anywhere in a chain without altering it
Note — an MPX cable carries no voltage, so a scope says nothing about it; this is the only way to read what is on one
Turns the chord arriving on an MPX stream into an arpeggio, playing its tones one at a time in time with the chart
Sets how often a note falls: once a bar, once in two beats, once a beat, or two, three or four a beat
Sets the order the tones are played in: up, down, up and down, random, or all at once as a chord
Sets how many octaves the figure climbs through before it starts again, one, two or three
Chooses how much of the chord is played: the triad, the sevenths, or every extension the chord has
Sets the register of the part, -24 to +24 semitones from middle C, which is how a musician states register whatever key the chart is in
Sets how long each note lasts as a percentage of its step; below 100% the notes are separated, at it they meet, above it they overlap
Chooses how loud each note is relative to the others: all the same, rising, falling, random, or first loudest
Bends each note after it has started, -2 to +2 semitones, and nought is off
Takes the note stream carrying the chord to play over
Carries the arpeggiated notes on as an MPX stream
Plays a chord accompaniment from the harmony on an MPX stream, with a choice of voicing, rhythmic figure and accent
Sets how many notes are sounded in each chord
Sets the register of the part, -24 to +24 semitones from middle C
Sets how wide the chord is spread, one, two or three octaves
Chooses whether the chord's root is sounded beneath it
Chooses the voicing: close, drop two, or open
Chooses how much of the chord is used: the triad, the sevenths, or the extensions
Sets how strongly each chord is voiced to move as little as possible from the one before it, 0 to 100%
Chooses between one held chord and a repeating rhythmic figure
Sets how often a step falls: once a bar, once in two beats, once a beat, or two, three or four a beat
Chooses the figure the notes are played in: block, broken upwards, broken downwards, Alberti, or waltz
Sets how much of each step a note fills, 5 to 100%
Chooses which steps are accented: evenly, by the metre, on the downbeat, on the backbeat, offbeat, or pushed
Sets how much louder an accented step is than the rest, 0 to 100%
Moves each note slightly off its exact time, 0 to 100%, so a figure does not sound mechanical
Spreads the notes of a chord over a few milliseconds instead of striking them together
Sets how the level is shared between the chord and the root beneath it, 0 to 100%
Takes the note stream carrying the harmony to play over
Carries the accompaniment on as an MPX stream
Generates four voices of euclidean rhythm as one MPX note stream, each voice with its own pattern, clock division and wandering level
Sets how many steps that voice's pattern is long, 1 to 32
Sets how many of that voice's steps sound, 0 to 32, spread as evenly through the pattern as they can be
Rotates that voice's pattern by a number of steps, 0 to 31, without changing which steps sound relative to each other
Sets how fast that voice is clocked relative to the incoming beat: every beat, half speed, a third or a quarter
Sets the level the voices wander around, 0 to 100%
Sets how far the level is allowed to wander from that setting, 0 to 100%
Sets the length of a note, 0.01 to 4 seconds, exponential so the short end has most of the travel
Sets how strongly a note's length follows its level, 0 to 100%, so louder notes can also be longer
Sets how fast the wandering moves, a quarter to sixteen beats per cycle
Sets how many beats pass before the wandering repeats itself, 1 to 64
Sets the tempo when no clock is patched, 30 to 300 beats per minute
Advances the patterns; patching anything here overrides the tempo knob
Returns every voice to the start of its pattern
Carries all four voices on as one MPX stream
Plays a chord progression as an MPX stream, so the modules downstream have a harmony to work against
Chooses which progression is played
Sets the key it is played in, the twelve semitones
Sets the tempo when no clock is patched, 30 to 300 beats per minute
Advances the progression; patching anything here overrides the tempo knob
Returns the progression to its first chord
Carries the progression on as an MPX stream
Varies one attribute of the notes passing through an MPX stream, leaving everything else as it arrived
Chooses which attribute is varied: duration, level, pan, timing or detune
Chooses the character of the variation: white, a random walk, or Perlin noise
Sets how far the attribute is moved, 0 to 100%, and at nought the notes come out exactly as they went in
Sets how fast the variation moves, 0.05 to 8 cycles per beat, and it means nothing for white
Chooses whether the variation repeats the same way each time round or is different on every pass
Takes the note stream to vary
Carries the varied notes on as an MPX stream
Plays a chord chart as an MPX stream and also as ordinary pitch voltages, so the harmony can drive modules that have no MPX input
Transposes the whole chart, -11 to +11 semitones
Sets the seed the chart's random choices are made from, 0 to 999, so a performance can be repeated exactly
Sets the tempo when no clock is patched, 30 to 300 beats per minute
Starts and stops playback
Returns the chart to its first bar
Chooses how the chord symbols are written
Opens the window where the chart itself is edited
Advances the chart; patching anything here overrides the tempo knob
Returns the chart to its first bar
Carries the chart's chords on as an MPX stream
Carries the tones of the chord in force as polyphonic pitch, one channel per tone
Carries the root of the chord in force as a pitch voltage
Carries a bass line beneath the chord as a pitch voltage
Note — the three pitch outputs are ordinary voltages, so a quantiser, an oscillator or anything else in the rack can be patched to the harmony without an MPX module in between
Mixes a polyphonic audio cable down to a stereo pair, with a level and a placing per channel
Sets the level applied to the first of the two level inputs, 0 to 100%
Sets the level applied to the second of the two level inputs, 0 to 100%
Sets the placing across the stereo field when nothing is patched to the pan input, hard left to hard right
Takes the polyphonic audio to be mixed down
Sets a level per channel, taken from one polyphonic cable
Sets a second level per channel, multiplied with the first
Sets the placing of each channel across the stereo field, one channel per voice
Carries the left side of the mix
Carries the right side of the mix
